selected_evidence.requirement: Configure opsadmin with the supplied public key
selected_evidence.summary: Shows account creation, secure paths, the requested RSA key fingerprint SHA256:SOtEda/YMy4/DAn3ColZo2z+LOEd2WbOIPn4KqW5/dc, locked password, one final key entry, and no temporary residue.
Effective policy requires `publickey` and disables passwords; live pre- and post-reboot tests show successful key login and rejection of non-key authentication.

selected_evidence.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline identifies RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64; the same kernel is running after reboot.

Healthy baseline boot ID was 9909e7e8-c083-4915-9e37-25fd616a539f; the native reboot was acknowledged; node1 returned with boot ID 38610d4b-27e8-43ea-9cf1-1ad7f4c44cae. Post-reboot evidence confirms system state running, sshd enabled/active/listening, valid configuration, recovered account/key data, correct policy, live key login, and non-key rejection.

commands.command:
set -eu
cfg=/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-key-only.conf
[ ! -e "$cfg" ] || { printf '%s\n' "$cfg already exists; refusing overwrite" >&2; exit 1; }
install -m 0600 -o root -g root /dev/null "$cfg"
trap 'rm -f "$cfg"' EXIT HUP INT TERM
printf '%s\n' '# Managed for key-only SSH access' 'PubkeyAuthentication yes' 'PasswordAuthentication no' 'KbdInteractiveAuthentication no' 'PermitEmptyPasswords no' 'AuthenticationMethods publickey' > "$cfg"
sshd -t
trap - EXIT HUP INT TERM
restorecon "$cfg"
systemctl reload sshd
systemctl is-active sshd
printf '%s\n' '--- installed policy ---'
cat "$cfg"
printf '%s\n' '--- effective global policy ---'
sshd -T | grep -E '^(pubkeyauthentication|passwordauthentication|kbdinteractiveauthentication|permitemptypasswords|authenticationmethods|usepam) '
printf '%s\n' '--- effective opsadmin policy ---'
sshd -T -C user=opsadmin,host=node1,addr="$NODE_IP" | grep -E '^(pubkeyauthentication|passwordauthentication|kbdinteractiveauthentication|permitemptypasswords|authenticationmethods|authorizedkeysfile) '

commands.command:
set -eu
td=$(mktemp -d /tmp/opsadmin-ssh-verify.XXXXXX)
keyfile=$td/id_ed25519
backup=$td/authorized_keys.requested
cp -p /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys "$backup"
cleanup() {
  cp -p "$backup" /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys 2>/dev/null || true
  chown opsadmin:opsadmin /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys 2>/dev/null || true
  chmod 0600 /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys 2>/dev/null || true
  restorecon /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  rm -rf "$td"
}
trap cleanup EXIT HUP INT TERM
ssh-keygen -q -t ed25519 -N '' -C opsadmin-temporary-verification -f "$keyfile"
cat "$keyfile.pub" >> /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys
chown opsadmin:opsadmin /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys
chmod 0600 /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys
printf '%s\n' '--- live public-key login test ---'
ssh -F /dev/null -i "$keyfile" -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o LogLevel=ERROR opsadmin@"$NODE_IP" 'printf "login-user="; id -un; printf "login-uid="; id -u'
printf '%s\n' '--- live non-key authentication rejection test ---'
set +e
deny_output=$(ssh -vv -F /dev/null -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -o PreferredAuthentications=password,keyboard-interactive,none -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null opsadmin@"$NODE_IP" true 2>&1)
deny_rc=$?
set -e
printf 'non-key-login-exit=%s\n' "$deny_rc"
printf '%s\n' "$deny_output" | grep -E 'Authentications that can continue|Permission denied' | tail -3 || true
[ "$deny_rc" -ne 0 ]
cleanup
trap - EXIT HUP INT TERM
printf '%s\n' '--- requested key restored after temporary test ---'
lines=$(grep -cEv '^[[:space:]]*(#|$)' /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys || true)
printf 'authorized-key-entries=%s\n' "$lines"
[ "$lines" -eq 1 ]
ssh-keygen -l -f /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys
stat -c '%U:%G %a %n' /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys
